Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3299 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

Recent findings suggest that “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

Sources indicate that “I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

Recent findings suggest that to say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

It has been revealed that the Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton stated after dodging that bullet.

It has been revealed that and although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It has been revealed that it could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

It has been revealed that could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My initiative is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

Recent findings suggest that he seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

It has been revealed that alpine managing director Steve Nielsen stated to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

It has been revealed that “We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Here’s what he remarked immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

According to recent reports, he states: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who remarked he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

It has been revealed that alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

According to recent reports, his tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Sources indicate that piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

According to recent reports, hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Recent findings suggest that verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

In a recent development, alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

Industry observers note that pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Sources indicate that monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Industry observers note that decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I remarked earlier.

Sources indicate that sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

Industry observers note that the Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car firm, isn’t there?

According to recent reports, 🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

Sources indicate that “Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

Industry observers note that “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

According to recent reports, A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM.

The pair are just natural friends.

In a recent development, max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT.

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton stated yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that “It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

It has been revealed that however, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

According to recent reports, perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista racconta perché aveva scelto la Spagna e l’accordo raggiunto con il club dopo lo stop.

L’esperienza di Matias Vecino al Celta Vigo, nella seconda parte della scorsa stagione, si è chiusa in anticipo dopo un infortunio al ginocchio. Secondo quanto riportato da Gianlucadimarzio, È stata, almeno per il momento, la sua ultima esperienza in campo. Il centrocampista ha raccontato la scelta di giocare in Spagna e l’accordo raggiunto con il club dopo lo stop.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nell’intervista a Gianlucadimarzio, Vecino ha spiegato che l’occasione si era presentata negli ultimi giorni, dopo una carriera trascorsa in Italia: «Ho fatto tutta la mia carriera qui in Italia, negli ultimi giorni si è presentata questa opportunità e ho deciso di coglierla.».

Il calcio spagnolo lo incuriosiva da tempo, anche per i racconti degli amici che vi avevano giocato: «Ero sempre stato curioso del calcio spagnolo, tanti amici avevano giocato lì e me ne avevano sempre parlato bene.» Vecino ha ricordato anche la situazione della squadra: «Al Celta poi c’era Marcos Alonso, poi erano arrivati agli ottavi di Europa League e stavano lottando per un posto in Europa».

Vecino ha descritto un modo di vivere il calcio diverso da quello italiano: «Forse un po’ più rilassato.» Ha aggiunto: «Cercano più il divertimento, oltre naturalmente alla vittoria.» E, a proposito della maggiore serenità, ha detto: «Vivono il calcio in maniera più serena.».

Tra le persone conosciute al Celta ha citato Giraldez, sul quale ha espresso un giudizio positivo: «Mi è piaciuto Giraldez, sentirete ancora parlare di lui».

In vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la 13ª giornata di campionato, l'infermeria porta diversi dubbi in casa granata. Come riportato da Toro News, Abate deve valutare vari acciacchi emersi dopo Napoli e situazioni da chiarire tra difesa e fasce, pur con qualche buona notizia, e le ultime indicazioni sul campionato arriveranno direttamente dalle parole del tecnico prima del match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Restano forti dubbi sull'impiego di Rafik Belghali contro la Lazio: il ginocchio destro infiammato (senza lesioni a menisco e legamenti) lo ha costretto al cambio al 40' al Maradona dopo aver stretto i denti al rientro anticipato dalla nazionale, e solo Abate chiarirà se potrà correre senza dolore. Stop più lungo per Ardian Ismajli: uscito nella ripresa a Napoli per una lesione di primo grado agli adduttori della coscia sinistra, salterà almeno tre settimane, a cui si somma l'operazione di osteosintesi alla mano destra per il quarto metacarpo che impone massima cautela.

According to recent reports, sulla sinistra resta in bilico Cristiano Biraghi, fermo a lavorare a parte per un affaticamento muscolare che lo staff valuterà giorno per giorno senza forzare, con convocazione incerta anche per la panchina. Segnali positivi invece da Niccolò Fortini, che ha superato la pubalgia ed è già tornato in panchina a Napoli: sta seguendo un percorso di potenziamento per ritrovare ritmo, e spetterà al tecnico decidere se impiegarlo con la Lazio o attendere ancora.

It has been revealed that il caso di Ricardo Rodriguez non è solo medico: dopo il recupero dall'infortunio pre Monza, ha risposto alla Svizzera giocando durante la sosta, attirando la dura reazione del Torino che lo ha escluso per motivi disciplinari a Napoli (scelta su cui Abate non ha avuto potere decisionale). Fisicamente sembra recuperato, ma resta da capire se verrà reintegrato per la sfida con i biancocelesti.

#165922. Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.
  • According to recent reports, what can he do to improve this shambles of a team?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

According to recent reports, what can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

Chief executive Omar Berrada said in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

It has been revealed that the game strategy was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone.

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped.

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Recent findings suggest that having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment.

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

Recent findings suggest that this is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

Latest Update: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • In a recent development, newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • It has been revealed that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

In a recent development, newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

It has been revealed that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

It has been revealed that ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Industry observers note that for the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

Sources indicate that “It shows where we have potential,” he remarked. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Recent findings suggest that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads indicated significant character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a fresh manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

Sources indicate that that opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another newly introduced signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

In a recent development, justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

Recent findings suggest that that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

According to recent reports, speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

According to recent reports, “We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads indicated the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV.

"Since the latest manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE.

It has been revealed that it’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

Industry observers note that the hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under upcoming head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Industry observers note that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Industry observers note that marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

Industry observers note that former Bundesliga striker Wout Weghorst has expressed his admiration for SC Freiburg’s remarkable development in recent years. The 34-year-old Dutch international, who previously represented VfL Wolfsburg and TSG Hoffenheim, returned to Germany with FC Twente for Thursday evening’s Conference League encounter at the Europa-Park Stadion.

Despite watching his side concede a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 2-1 defeat, Weghorst was full of praise for the Bundesliga club’s progress.

Industry observers note that “Respect, just simply respect,” Weghorst noted when asked about Freiburg’s scintillating form by Kicker’s Carsten Schröter-Lorenz in the mixed zone afterwards. “I spoke of respect before the game as well. When I was here [in Germany] playing for Wolfsburg and then later at Hoffenheim they were more of a mid-table team. One has beheld a simply amazing development in the last years. Praise to them for that. They’re on a good track.”.

In a recent development, weghorst became familiar with Freiburg during his four seasons at Wolfsburg between 2018 and 2022 and his subsequent loan spell at Hoffenheim during the 2023/24 campaign. The Schwarzwaldverein were already establishing themselves as regular contenders for European qualification during that period, but their continued progress has since carried them to even greater heights.

Freiburg reached their first European final last season, eventually losing to Aston Villa in the Europa League showpiece in Istanbul. The club nevertheless secured another season of European football and entered the current campaign with a revamped squad.

As Get German Football News examined extensively in our 2026/27 Freiburg tactical preview, the club’s ability to navigate significant departures, reinvest intelligently, and maintain tactical continuity has remained central to its success.

Freiburg’s current European campaign has offered further evidence of that progress. Following November’s hard-fought Conference League victory over Trabzonspor, Schuster’s men have now extended their remarkable home-winning streak in European competition to 14 matches.

Thursday’s contest against Twente was hardly straightforward. The Dutch visitors enjoyed the better of the opening half despite conceding an early goal to Cyriaque Irié. Younes Taha’s superb second-half free kick eventually brought Twente level before substitute Niklas Beste struck in stoppage time to secure Freiburg’s sixth consecutive competitive victory.

The result also kept alive the European ambitions that Schuster and Vincenzo Grifo discussed following the club’s Conference League opener against FK Jablonec. Freiburg’s supporters have made no secret of their hopes for another deep continental run after last season’s historic adventure.

For Weghorst, the progress is unmistakable. The former Bundesliga striker may have departed Freiburg empty-handed on Thursday evening, but his assessment of the club’s remarkable transformation was unequivocally positive.

Germany international Noted El Mala believes his developing partnership with Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore still has considerable room for improvement. The 20-year-old Cologne attacker has spoken enthusiastically about his understanding with the English youngster following their successful attacking combination in last weekend’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Bayern Munich.

It has been revealed that moore, 19, scored his first Bundesliga goal in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena, rounding Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after receiving a return pass from El Mala. The well-worked goal provided a welcome breakthrough for the Englishman following a difficult start to his loan spell in Germany.

As Get German Football News reported following the Bayern encounter, Moore expressed relief at finally opening his Bundesliga account and discussed the growing understanding between himself and El Mala.

The partnership has been a topic of considerable interest ever since Moore arrived from Tottenham in August. Cologne head coach René Wagner spoke of his enthusiasm for the attacking combination back in September, emphasizing that the two youngsters were not competing for one exclusive place in the team. Moore himself subsequently expressed his desire to develop a stronger understanding with El Mala ahead of October’s Rhein derby against Borussia Mönchengladbach.

According to recent reports, the friendship also extends beyond the training ground, with El Mala revealing that his older brother Malek has spent time with Moore as well. Speaking in an extensive interview with Kicker, the 20-year-old described their growing bond.

“Malek and I get on really well with Mikey,” El Mala told Kicker. “The three of us recently went out for a meal together. We get along very well. Now he’s scored his first goal after a great attacking move, which gives us confidence for the coming matches that we can play together like that. I also have a very good relationship with Linton Maina, for example, and you can see that on the pitch.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September.
  • Sources indicate that kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football. According to Kicker, the 23-year-old appears to have aggravated the muscle injury that previously sidelined him for nearly two months. The German international will consequently miss Saturday’s Bundesliga away fixture against Hamburger SV.

Musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September. After gradually working his way back to fitness, the Bayern star finally returned to competitive action in last Friday’s 1-1 draw against Köln. He also made a brief appearance in Wednesday’s 2-1 Champions League defeat against Lille.

Sources indicate that kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear. Fußballtransfers claims Musiala’s absence will stretch out for several more weeks. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg is reporting that Musiala will miss 4-6 weeks.

Recent findings suggest that the latest development comes during an exceptionally difficult period for Musiala, who has also been dealing with a neurological condition. Kicker and Sport Bild both report that the 23-year-old experienced another absence episode on Monday, November 23, his second reported recurrence since collapsing during August’s preparation campaign. Musiala has consequently made just six competitive appearances this season, completing the full 90 minutes on only one occasion.

His ongoing health difficulties have also prompted considerable discussion surrounding his future at Bayern. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge recently expressed concerns about the midfielder’s ability to regain his previous performance levels. Earlier this week, Bayern also confirmed that constructive discussions had taken place with Musiala’s representatives. The club emphasized that the player’s health remained the priority and that both parties intended to continue their dialogue confidentially.

For Kompany, Musiala’s latest absence also creates another selection headache amid a mounting injury crisis in Bayern’s attacking department. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of Saturday’s encounter with Hamburg. The French international continues to recover from bruising to his left foot sustained against Köln. Harry Kane, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari remain sidelined as well, leaving Bayern seriously depleted in attack. Luis Díaz at least returned to action against Lille following his own injury layoff.

I was in the room with Newcastle bosses as they were grilled by fans on Matthias Jaissle, their January transfer plans and the fresh stadium - here's what they had to say, and my verdict: CRAIG HOPE

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1472 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.
  • Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a new stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.

Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.

Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a new stadium.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics….

According to recent reports, ‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

Industry observers note that ‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

Recent findings suggest that ‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday.

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal.

HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a strategy that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were notable contributors to the past season.

In a recent development, ‘We set out on a direction under Ross' leadership where we would have a different set of expectations that recognised financial reality. We articulated a vision for the squad here that would be organised around some young talent, who we expect to grow here.

‘So I’m delighted with the job Ross did. We executed that strategy superbly. Not everything that we set out to do was accomplished. We went hard on Johan Manzambi and didn't succeed. We went hard on Victor Munoz, didn't succeed, despite thinking we were going to land both of those at one point. But also had successes that we had not anticipated.’.

According to recent reports, HOPE: Wilson also spoke about the strategy of bringing down the squad’s average age, and there appeared to be no panic or concern over the so-far indifferent impact of summer additions. It has been noted by many that on Saturday, in the second half, no new signings were involved apart from goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. For me, you cannot judge players over three months (look at Lewis Hall) but the substantial price tags attached to some of the young arrivals has raised expectation. Jaissle and the hierarchy need the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, in particular, to start impacting, if questions over summer business are to quieten.

’In simple terms, the club had maxed out its credit card in the first few years under the new ownership. We had complied with PSR but it had been incredibly tight, and that forced us to sell at an undervalued price people like Elliot Anderson. We didn’t want to and we didn't want to be there again.

Industry observers note that ‘So we had to do something differently. The good news is that the Premier League has changed their rules so that there's a bit more headroom now. We’re comfortably within those and we're also comfortably within what we've agreed with UEFA (Newcastle were fined earlier this year). So we're in a really good place. That's the work that David and Ross had talked about in terms of 2.0.

‘That allows us to actually continue to invest and trade. It means that we've got no imperative to sell somebody in January. And it gives us the ability, depending on where we are in the league at the end of this season, to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.’.

It has been revealed that HOPE: The message was clear - there is scope to spend in January and next summer. Newcastle should use that to target goals in the New Year.

New Magpies coach Mathias Jaissle was also under the microscope in the shadow of St James' Park.

‘Eddie Howe was a workaholic and he put his heart and soul into the job. So we needed someone who would work hard and the players would not notice a drop off. Matthias works incredibly hard.

‘Eddie was also outstanding on the grass, an elite coach. Again, our players couldn't feel, “Eddie’s gone and they've got another guy who doesn't coach”. Matthias is an expert, elite coach.

Recent findings suggest that ‘From a transfer perspective, the head coach at Newcastle always has the final say in any player who comes in. Matthias puts a lot of effort into that - convincing players and making sure they're the right character fit for him. He’s thrown himself into all things Newcastle and we enjoy working with him a lot.’.

‘Matthias is a clear winner. And you know winners, they win over time. I have a high, high conviction we're going to win under his leadership. I don't think I've ever had the conviction more that we're going to win together than I do right now.’.

HOPE: It is a bold statement from Hopkinson on the back of one win in seven, but the support for Jaissle is clear. He will (and should) be given time, despite an inconsistent start that has included a couple of horror highlights. It was also interesting to note Wilson’s reference to Jaissle’s heavy involvement in transfers, on the back of a week in which the head coach let it be known he wanted more control over transfers.

It has been revealed that ‘This decision is going to last forever. It will outlast our lifetime. It’s that enormity that means we are taking a little bit of time now.

Industry observers note that ‘Is it going to allow us to compete with the top clubs? Are we going to be able to do it from a financial perspective? Is it going to be transformative for all of our fans, the city and for the region? For all of those reasons, we are very purposely taking our time. But whether we stay at St James’ Park or move, it will be absolutely fantastic.’.

Newcastle continue to mull key decisions on the renovation of their stadium in a bid to unlock new revenue for the club.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We need it (larger stadium) for the revenue a upcoming stadium will unlock. This is a generational decision and will define the next era of this club. It’s going to be really expensive. We’re advancing significantly into clearly defined options. This is a project with global significance.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We've spent a lot of time with New York bankers recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider. I can assure you we're working on this every day. I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon.’.

HOPE: There was ‘no revision’ but the subtext of the discussion was very definitely geared towards a latest stadium. I understand this is the direction of travel now, and Hopkinson confirming our story from last week about the high-level talks with Goldman Sachs over how to finance a new stadium demonstrates how advanced the project is.

According to recent reports, overall, the tone of the night was one of ‘we have a proposal, stick with us’. It was very different 12 months ago, when the mood in the room was one of huge optimism and excitement at the unveiling of a new executive team ahead of a Champions League campaign.

Now, it feels like all involved - supporters and those on the inside - realise that this part of the journey will not be easy. That was reflected in the message conveyed.

ANALYSIS | Eric Smith: Meet of the 2. Bundesliga’s smartest players, and why St. Pauli need him

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ever since becoming an crucial player for St.
  • Under Fabian Hürzeler, he played a hybrid role, combining the positions of centre back and holding midfielder.
  • He received a lot of praise for mastering this role, which was linked to a transfer to a bigger club, such as VfB Stuttgart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ever since becoming an crucial player for St. Pauli, Eric Smith has enjoyed successful seasons.

Under Fabian Hürzeler, he played a hybrid role, combining the positions of centre back and holding midfielder. During those successful periods, he controlled and directed St. Pauli’s attack. His movement destroyed the opponent’s initial press and his passing cracked defensive structures, starting his team’s attack.

He received a lot of praise for mastering this role, which was linked to a transfer to a bigger club, such as VfB Stuttgart. However, he decided to stay.

According to recent reports, under Alexander Blessin, he sometimes played as a number six and more frequently as a central centre-back. Although he didn’t have the freedom to move around as much as before, he was still dictating the tempo, and his long balls played a more integral part in St. Pauli’s direct attack. However, during Blessin’s time at the club, the Kiezkicker were more passive offensively, so Smith’s role was more highlighting the defensive part.

In a recent development, in that role, though, he delivered some good performances, especially in their first Bundesliga season, and was consistently solid defensively. Once again, he was linked with a transfer, this time to Leicester City in England. And once again, Eric Smith decided to stay.

Recent findings suggest that the following season, after St. Pauli were relegated to the 2. Bundesliga, there were rumours that Smith was about to leave. He was linked with Belgian giants Anderlecht, but the move never materialised.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, he has continued to perform well, even though his team has not been as consistent. In the summer, Graham Potter selected him for the Sweden national team at the World Cup. Even though he has shown some flaws, particularly in duels, his performances suggest that he might be too good for the 2. Bundesliga. He might be a better fit for a higher league.

And so far this season, this has been proven true. Even though St. Pauli haven’t really been consistent, Smith has been performing well from matchday to matchday.

The data also indicates this. According to Ben Griffis’s measurements, Smith is at the moment in the top five of the 2. Bundesliga for three different midfield roles (number six, defensive midfielder and advanced playmaker). No other midfielder can be in the top five in all of these categories.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of passing and chance creation via passes in the 2. Bundesliga, he is also categorised as either elite (top 10%) or above average.

According to recent reports, not only that. Among 2. midfielders in the Bundesliga who have played at least 900 minutes so far this season, none are averaging more progressive passes or passes to the final third per 90 minutes than Smith. He is arguably still the best build-up player and progressor in the league. This is precisely why St. Pauli need him.

With all these numbers, it no longer makes sense to play Smith in the centre-back position. He is very familiar with this position, though, and Tim Eckhardt from Millernton also explained to me that one reason he is still playing in this position might due to the reason that he can provide reassurance to the defensive team, particularly the other centre-backs who don’t have as much experience as him. Smith himself also admits that he doesn’t feel as comfortable playing in the final third as he does at the back. However, he is needed more as a midfielder to support the team’s attack, an area in which St. Pauli has struggled this season.

The last game against Bochum proved this. Smith not only made one assist, but also created five chances in total (the most in the game). He was everywhere, ensuring that St. Pauli’s attack ran smoothly — he is the glue holding the team’s offensive play together.

It has been revealed that after the game, he stated that his movements, particularly on the right side of the final third, were intended to help St. Pauli break through Bochum’s man-to-man defence. Smith’s intelligence was evident in his ability to anticipate where to move, where to meet or reach his teammate, and where to pass the ball. This approach was successful in breaking down Bochum’s defensive structure.

This kind of vision was lacking when coach Marcel Rapp decided to play Smith as a centre-back in some games this season. With St. Pauli presently sitting in the middle of the table, that shouldn’t happen again. Smith needs to be their main creative outlet at the front.

Recent findings suggest that in general, Smith is also third in terms of key passes per 90 minutes for his side this season, averaging 1.5 and only behind two playmakers Conor Metcalfe and Branimir Hrgota–which have most of their minutes playing in the final third. If these three, or at least two, players on the field together at the same time for the rest of season, St. Pauli might find the cure to solve their creative flaws.

Things also work quite well because Smith has a very good understanding with his midfield partner, Joel Fujita. The Japanese player knows how to cover ground when Smith is in the final third, and also knows when to get close to the ball when Smith needs help.

According to recent reports, well, they both have qualities that many would argue are better than the 2. Bundesliga level. Keeping them as a double-six duet would give St. Pauli one of the best midfield partnerships in the league.

Having a great midfield partnership, especially if both players are above league average, usually helps a team achieve better results. St. Pauli can certainly hope for this. It might slightly reduce their defensive quality, but to win a game you need to score more goals than your opponents–something that St. Pauli has really lacked this season.

In a recent development, it may also be beneficial for their captain, David Nemeth, to take on more defensive responsibilities and become a true leader in that regard. It might also help Tomoya Ando and new recruit Marcus Mathisen to settle in and prove that they can become top defenders in the league.

St. Pauli are not a middle-bottom 2. Bundesliga squad; they have players capable of elevating the team. They just need to make wiser decisions, and one of them is keeping Smith closer to the final third for the rest of the season.

Daniel Heuer Fernandes – Sebastiaan Bornauw, Mario Vušković, Warmed Omari – Zakaria El Ouahdi, Nicolás Capaldo, Martin Adeline, David Møller Wolfe – Albert Grønbæk – Patson Daka, Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany international Said El Mala has opened up about the setbacks, family influences, and personal decisions that have shaped his remarkable rise to prominence.
  • El Mala’s development has been extraordinary.
  • According to recent reports, football has always played a central role in the El Mala family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany international Said El Mala has opened up about the setbacks, family influences, and personal decisions that have shaped his remarkable rise to prominence. In an extensive interview with Kicker, the 20-year-old 1. FC Köln attacker reflected on his painful departure from Borussia Mönchengladbach’s youth academy, his unwavering determination to become a professional footballer, and his decision to reject opportunities elsewhere in favour of remaining in the cathedral city.

El Mala’s development has been extraordinary. Released from Gladbach at the age of 14, the Krefeld native subsequently worked his way through TSV Meerbusch and Viktoria Köln before establishing himself as one of the Bundesliga’s most exciting young players. His performances have since earned him a place in Jürgen Klopp’s German national team. The youngster nevertheless admits that his career came perilously close to ending before it had properly begun.

According to recent reports, football has always played a central role in the El Mala family. Mentioned’s father Mohammed previously played for Linner SV, helping the amateur club climb as high as the Landesliga. Unlike his two attacking sons, Mohammed operated primarily in central defence.

Sources indicate that “No!” El Mala laughed when asked whether he inherited his attacking talent from his father. “My father was actually a centre-back. He played a lot as a sweeper, from what he’s told me. What I always heard from his former opponents was that he was a really unpleasant player to face. Someone you didn’t want to play against because he was so tall and quick. But our dad naturally still played a part in Malek and me both becoming attacking players.”.

Sources indicate that the brothers’ own footballing journey took them from Linner SV through KFC Uerdingen to Borussia Mönchengladbach. Their development then suffered a devastating setback when Gladbach decided to release them in 2021. As Get German Football News previously documented in our feature on El Mala’s journey from Gladbach reject to Germany international, the youngster was considered too small and physically underdeveloped to establish himself at the highest level. El Mala has now provided a deeply personal account of the experience, explaining that the coronavirus pandemic, injuries, and his physical development all contributed to the difficulties he encountered.

It has been revealed that “I was 14 when I was kicked out,” El Mala told Kicker. “During the coronavirus period, there were no opportunities to show what you could do. There were also injuries. I was physically weaker and still very small. Looking back on it today, it was a very difficult time.”.

Sources indicate that the decision was particularly devastating because El Mala had sacrificed much of his social life to pursue his footballing ambitions. His older brother’s encouragement ultimately helped preserve a footballing career that might otherwise have ended prematurely.

According to recent reports, “When the news came, I didn’t know how to deal with it,” he explained. “At the academy, I’d had to neglect my friends from school because I didn’t have time to meet them after lessons or go to their birthdays. It was a completely new life. The new friends were the lads from the team. Then, out of nowhere, you’re simply torn away from it. There were a few tears shed. But then Malek and I decided that we did want to carry on playing, simply for fun. Though the decision came more from Malek.”.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding his future, El Mala remained determined to become a professional footballer. The attacker revealed that he briefly considered following a completely different career path, but never seriously entertained the prospect of abandoning his original ambitions.

“I once wanted to become a police officer,” El Mala admitted. “But that thought quickly disappeared because I only wanted to pursue Plan A. The teachers always told me that I needed a Plan B, but I remarked no. I’ve always been stubborn, and I’ve followed my own path. At first, it was simply about seeing Plan A through.”.

It has been revealed that that determination eventually paid off. Following a spell at Meerbusch, El Mala earned an opportunity with Viktoria Köln, where his development accelerated under youth coach Marian Wilhelm. The winger subsequently earned a move to 1. FC Cologne, making the transition to Bundesliga football alongside his older brother.

The siblings’ shared journey reached another milestone earlier this month when Malek scored his first Bundesliga goal in Cologne’s 1-1 draw against Union Berlin. The 21-year-old striker converted shortly after coming off the bench, with Noted involved in creating the equalizer.

After scoring 13 Bundesliga goals and providing five assists last season, El Mala attracted considerable transfer interest during the summer. Brentford, Brighton & Hove Albion, and Borussia Dortmund were among the clubs attempting to secure his services. Dortmund’s interest became particularly serious, with Cologne reportedly rejecting multiple offers from the Bundesliga rivals.

Sources indicate that instead of leaving, El Mala signed a latest contract through 2031 and inherited the prestigious No. 10 shirt previously worn by club legends Lukas Podolski, Pierre Littbarski, and Wolfgang Overath. The German international has now explained the reasoning behind his decision.

“We were actually in talks with FC the whole time,” El Mala told Kicker. “It’s no secret that I received offers and listened to them. But I couldn’t really imagine myself making any of those moves. Then we sat down together, my family, the club officials, and me, and talked. They showed me something that really appealed to me: the team structure, who else they wanted to bring in, and how we wanted to play under the coach. That was what ultimately convinced me. We’ve added real quality.”.

It has been revealed that the opportunity to inherit Podolski’s famous shirt number also played an important role. As GGFN reported following El Mala’s first Bundesliga home appearance in the iconic shirt, the youngster has acknowledged the considerable expectations that accompany his latest status in Cologne. His brother’s future also influenced his decision to remain.

The attacker’s mother Sabrina, who also acts as his agent, was closely involved in the discussions. El Mala stressed that the family’s decision was ultimately based on their shared conviction that remaining in Cologne represented the best next step in his development.

In a recent development, “I chose Cologne,” El Mala emphasized. “I’ve felt incredibly comfortable with the lads from the very first day. We brought in a lot of fresh players over the summer and lost quite a few, but we haven’t lost quality. We’ve actually gained it. My brother was also one of the reasons, because I was certain he would get his opportunity this year and that things would finally click for him. The fact that it worked out and he scored straight away in Berlin made me all the happier.”.

It has been revealed that el Mala’s confidence in the club’s sporting direction also extends to head coach René Wagner, whose position has come under increasing scrutiny following Köln’s difficult start to the Bundesliga campaign. With just ten points from their opening ten league matches, the Rhineland club have struggled for consistency. Wagner has faced considerable criticism from sections of the support, with thousands of fans chanting for his dismissal following the recent goalless draw against Schalke. Wagner’s position had already become a subject of debate earlier in the season.

El Mala nevertheless remains firmly behind his trainer. The German international highlighted Wagner’s communication skills and individual attention to players, revealing that the coach regularly invites him to his office to review running statistics and video footage of his performances. The 20-year-old also cited Köln’s recent 1-1 draw away against Bayern Munich as evidence that Wagner and his coaching staff remain capable of preparing the team to compete with the Bundesliga’s strongest opponents.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone has a good relationship with him,” El Mala told Kicker. “He talks a lot with all of us, which is particularly key when you’re not playing or when you’re trying to improve. We work with video analysis very frequently. There are many things that distinguish him. We played a great game against Bayern. The entire coaching staff worked out a great match plan, which we implemented really well. If we function like that, all together as a team, we can compete against any other team and deliver that kind of performance in every match. I don’t right now see any reason to criticize the coach.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, TSG Hoffenheim have officially appealed the four-match suspension handed to Turkish international Ozan Kabak following his dismissal against Eintracht Frankfurt. According to Kicker, the 26-year-old defender’s case will be heard by the DFB sports court on Friday, December 4.

Kabak received a straight red card in stoppage time after grabbing and pushing Frankfurt midfielder Oscar Højlund in retaliation for a heavy challenge. The subsequent four-match ban would rule the centre-back out of Hoffenheim’s remaining Bundesliga fixtures before the winter break.

The Kraichgauer hope to have the suspension reduced to three matches, which would allow Kabak to return for their final league encounter of 2026 against Union Berlin. The DFB sports court could nevertheless also impose a harsher punishment following the hearing.

Recent findings suggest that the appeal comes at a particularly difficult time for head coach Christian Ilzer, who has just one fit specialist centre-back available in Koki Machida. Dutch midfielder Wouter Burger had been considered as a potential emergency replacement, but suffered an abdominal muscle injury during Thursday’s Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz.

Ilzer has nevertheless emphasized that Kabak retains his full confidence despite the disciplinary incident.

Recent findings suggest that “Ozan is someone I really enjoy working with,” Ilzer remarked after the Europa League tie. “He’s extremely reliable and always gives everything he has in a match. I’ve discussed it with him at length, and there has also been a consequence. Nevertheless, Ozan won’t lose my trust. He doesn’t need to make amends. He simply needs to learn from this situation.”.

Kabak will begin serving his suspension when Hoffenheim host Augsburg on Sunday evening.

Unusual Mikey Moore loan clause could save Cologne €1.5m

💡 Key Takeaways
  • FC Cologne could end up paying virtually nothing in loan fees for Tottenham Hotspur attacker Mikey Moore thanks to an unusual clause in the 19-year-old’s agreement.
  • Moore’s season-long loan could theoretically cost Cologne as much as €1.5 million in loan fees.
  • Recent findings suggest that cologne would then effectively be responsible only for the player’s wages.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FC Cologne could end up paying virtually nothing in loan fees for Tottenham Hotspur attacker Mikey Moore thanks to an unusual clause in the 19-year-old’s agreement. According to a report appearing in the Wednesday print edition of Sport Bild, the Bundesliga club’s financial obligations decrease considerably depending on how frequently the English youngster features for René Wagner’s team.

Moore’s season-long loan could theoretically cost Cologne as much as €1.5 million in loan fees. The agreement nevertheless contains a provision that reduces the fee with each qualifying appearance. Should Moore make 28 competitive appearances featuring at least 45 minutes on the pitch, the payment to Tottenham would drop to its lowest possible level.

Recent findings suggest that cologne would then effectively be responsible only for the player’s wages. As of Wednesday, November 25, Moore had already accumulated eight appearances meeting the required playing-time threshold.

The arrangement provides an obvious incentive for Cologne to continue giving Moore regular playing time, while Tottenham stand to benefit from the youngster gaining valuable Bundesliga experience. Cologne did not negotiate a purchase option as part of the agreement. Tottenham reportedly intend to incorporate the England youth international into their first-team looks for the 2027/28 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that the latest revelations also offer additional context to recent speculation concerning a possible premature termination of Moore’s loan. Cologne sporting director Thomas Kessler and head coach René Wagner have consistently emphasized their confidence in the youngster despite his initial difficulties adapting to German football.

It has been revealed that that patience finally began to pay dividends last Friday when Moore scored his first Bundesliga goal in Cologne’s impressive 1-1 draw against Bayern Munich. The teenager rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after combining with Said El Mala to give the visitors an early lead. Moore subsequently spoke of his relief at ending his wait for a Bundesliga goal, while El Mala expressed optimism about the pair’s developing attacking partnership.

With Moore showing signs of improvement, the financial structure of his loan offers Cologne another reason to continue investing in his development. Tottenham, meanwhile, stand to regain a more experienced player next summer without having surrendered control over his long-term future.

Latest Update: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?
  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
