Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.
  • Recent findings suggest that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window.
  • It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Recent findings suggest that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

Sources indicate that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

It has been revealed that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” stated David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Industry observers note that benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

According to recent reports, but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

Recent findings suggest that how had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

Recent findings suggest that it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

It has been revealed that when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

Industry observers note that "That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

According to recent reports, “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes mentioned. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

According to recent reports, they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

It has been revealed that as Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq.

Recent findings suggest that it felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It has been revealed that it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

Sources indicate that I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Sources indicate that even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Sources indicate that just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

Recent findings suggest that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

Industry observers note that grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”.

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

According to recent reports, everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

According to recent reports, as Dominic states, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

According to recent reports, "That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

According to recent reports, free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Industry observers note that maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

Recent findings suggest that george has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

According to recent reports, “He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Sources indicate that rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

In a recent development, johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Industry observers note that mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Can’t be long before Grealish comes on.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh.

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

According to recent reports, both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

According to recent reports, brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Sources indicate that rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

In a recent development, everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Industry observers note that branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

In a recent development, fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

It has been revealed that now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

It has been revealed that dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Substantial shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

According to recent reports, slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

In a recent development, speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

Industry observers note that david Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having remarked that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo la vittoria per 2-0 in Champions League contro lo Stoccarda, l’Inter si prepara a tornare in campo in campionato per ospitare il Genoa nel primo dei due impegni che vedranno i nerazzurri fronteggiare i rossoblu nel giro di quattro giorni: sabato 29 novembre le due squadre si affronteranno nel 13° turno di Serie A, mentre martedì 1° dicembre si ritroveranno a San Siro per gli ottavi di finale di Coppa Italia.

Recent findings suggest that la squadra allenata da Daniele De Rossi occupa attualmente il decimo posto in classifica con 16 punti, frutto di cinque vittorie, un pareggio e sei sconfitte, con 13 gol realizzati e 16 subiti. Un avversario che ha alternato momenti di difficoltà a prestazioni convincenti, ma che nelle ultime settimane ha dimostrato di aver trovato compattezza e di essere in grado di colpire gli avversari con le proprie armi migliori.

Il Genoa non è una squadra che cerca necessariamente di imporre il proprio gioco attraverso il possesso palla. Con una media del 42,6%, i liguri sono tra le formazioni che mantengono meno a lungo il pallone in Serie A, al 17° posto nella graduatoria del possesso medio. La manovra si sviluppa spesso attraverso passaggi verticali e palloni diretti verso il reparto offensivo: i rossoblù sono infatti la squadra che tenta più lanci lunghi nel campionato, con una media di 52,5 a partita.La ricerca della profondità e delle seconde palle rappresenta quindi una componente importante del gioco di De Rossi. Una volta conquistato il possesso, il Genoa cerca di risalire rapidamente il campo, sfruttando soprattutto i movimenti degli attaccanti e gli inserimenti dei centrocampisti. Le corsie sono un'altra risorsa importante, con gli esterni accompagnano frequentemente l'azione e contribuiscono alla costruzione offensiva.

In fase di non possesso, il Genoa alterna momenti di pressione più aggressiva a una disposizione compatta nella propria metà campo. Il sistema a tre centrali permette di avere una buona presenza numerica nella zona difensiva e di proteggere l'area, mentre i centrocampisti sono chiamati a lavorare con intensità per recuperare il pallone e interrompere le linee di passaggio avversarie.La formazione rossoblù si distingue anche per l'intensità nei duelli: è terza in Serie A per contrasti tentati, con una media di 18,3 a partita, e per duelli a terra vinti (54%). Numeri che descrivono una squadra combattiva, aggressiva e pronta a rendere fisico il confronto con gli avversari.

Industry observers note that il rendimento offensivo resta uno degli aspetti sui quali De Rossi può trovare margini di miglioramento. Con 13 reti segnate in dodici giornate, il Genoa viaggia a una media di 1,08 gol a partita. Anche la produzione offensiva evidenzia alcune difficoltà: la squadra produce circa 1,0 xG a partita e registra una media di 11,7 conclusioni, delle quali soltanto 3,3 nello specchio della porta. Un dato che colloca i rossoblù nelle ultime posizioni del campionato per tiri in porta.Allo stesso tempo, il Genoa concede agli avversari una media di 16 conclusioni a partita, a testimonianza di una fase difensiva che non sempre riesce a impedire agli avversari di arrivare alla conclusione. La squadra ha però dimostrato di poter trovare maggiore equilibrio quando riesce a mantenere compattezza tra i reparti e a sfruttare gli spazi in transizione.

Il successo contro la Juventus e quello più recente sul Sassuolo sono indicazioni importanti: il Genoa ha dimostrato di poter essere particolarmente efficace quando riesce a difendere con ordine e a sfruttare la qualità dei propri uomini offensivi nelle ripartenze.

In a recent development, alle sue spalle, Tommaso Baldanzi è uno degli interpreti più pericolosi sulla trequarti. Tecnica, rapidità nello stretto e capacità di giocare tra le linee sono le sue caratteristiche principali. Ha già realizzato due gol e servito due assist in campionato, confermandosi un elemento chiave nella creazione delle trame offensive. Tra le linee agisce anche Junior Messias, che può agire da esterno offensivo o da trequartista, e mette a disposizione qualità individuale, dribbling e un mancino pericoloso, con cui cerca spesso la conclusione accentrandosi dalla fascia: il brasiliano ha già realizzato due reti e servito un assist in questa stagione. Un’alternativa duttile in avanti è rappresentata da Vitinha, elemento in grado di agire sia da centravanti che da seconda punta grazie alla sua velocità e alla capacità di allargarsi per fare gioco, mentre Stephan El Shaarawy, rappresenta un'importante alternativa offensiva grazie alla sua esperienza e alla capacità di muoversi tra fascia e zona centrale.

According to recent reports, sulle corsie e in mezzo al campo spicca Mikael Ellertsson, tra i giocatori più utilizzati da De Rossi, con dodici presenze su dodici in questo campionato. L'islandese garantisce corsa, intensità e disponibilità al lavoro in entrambe le fasi. Ha già segnato due gol e fornito un assist, dimostrando di poter essere pericoloso anche negli inserimenti senza palla.

Il centrocampo può contare anche su Morten Frendrup, elemento fondamentale per equilibrio e recupero del pallone. Il danese è uno dei principali interpreti del lavoro di interdizione, grazie alla sua aggressività nei contrasti e alla capacità di coprire ampie porzioni di campo. Accanto a lui, la presenza di Hamed Junior Traorè garantisce ulteriore fisicità e dinamismo.

Industry observers note that in difesa, Leo Østigård è il riferimento per presenze, solidità e impostazione. Sempre titolare nelle prime dodici giornate, il centrale norvegese è anche il giocatore del Genoa con più passaggi riusciti in campionato (386). Al suo fianco, Johan Vásquez porta esperienza e aggressività, oltre a una buona capacità di lettura delle situazioni difensive. Alessandro Marcandalli rappresenta un profilo duttile, capace di giocare sia come terzo centrale che come esterno, mentre Kingsley Ehizibue garantisce spinta e corsa sulla fascia.

  • Enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere.
  • According to recent reports, I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere. Prendiamo il punto, ne abbiamo 10 in classifica e in fin dei conti è un buon risultato per andare avanti. Ricordo un loro calcio d’angolo e i due gol, in questo momento gli avversari sono cinici davanti alla porta. C’è poco da fare, accettiamo il punto e andiamo avanti. L’impatto sui giocatori? In questo momento va un po’ così, le prime dieci partite siamo stati sempre noi a sbloccare, mentre ora sono gli avversari a farlo. Non credo che abbia un impatto sulla fiducia dei calciatori, devi correre un po’ di più se sei in svantaggio, ma abbiamo lottato fino alla fine e serve alzare l’asticella. Non dobbiamo subire questi gol, basta vedere le statistiche a nostro favore. C’è uno squilibrio tra le occasioni create e i gol segnati. Anche Cherki ha detto che mancava energia? Siamo stati molto aggressivi. I due terzini in posizione centrale? Abbiamo iniziato con Bouaddi e Enzo in mezzo per vedere se potevamo trovare equilibrio, poi Nico e Matheus Nunes hanno fatto bene, è un’altra opzione per noi. Volevamo fare qualche cambio ed essere più fisici in mezzo al campo per contrastarli. La qualità del gol di Cherki? Ottimo, sono contento per lui. Ha fatto bene, sappiamo che sa giocare meglio centralmente, ma sta facendo bene. Ci aspettavamo un Napoli col blocco basso, era difficile trovare soluzioni, ma dovevamo evitare di concedere i gol concessi, erano evitabili. I cori a Donnarumma? Non ci ho fatto caso, ero concentrato sulla partita. Era difficile attaccare il Napoli, erano in undici sulla linea dell’area. Potevamo fare meglio nelle chance avute e cercare di evitare le due occasioni concesse. Hanno avuto quelle e il corner di Beukema, c’è rammarico per non aver vinto, ma se non puoi farlo è importante anche non perdere. Non vinciamo da tre partite, ma i meriti del Napoli sono importanti: si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni. Noi potevamo fare meglio, il Napoli ha avuto i suoi meriti e ha fatto una buona gara”.

  • Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.
  • The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

According to recent reports, ‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

According to recent reports, there's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

It has been revealed that ‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that highlights in his play,' claims Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

Industry observers note that to make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that demonstrates in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

In a recent development, intervenuto a Cronache di Spogliatoio, Fabrizio Biasin, giornalista, ha parlato così della vittoria dell'Inter di Cristian Chivu contro lo Stoccarda: "Cosa manca all'Inter? Dipende qual è il termine di paragone: di cosa stiamo parlando? Dell'Inter che batte il Bayern con Inzaghi? E' un'altra squadra: ricordiamoci che è una squadra che viene da 7 sconfitte in 8 partite in Champions e adesso è alla terza vittoria di fila. Con una partita molto solida, non bellissima: doveva dare una risposta rispetto ad una marea di critiche arrivate nelle ultime ore. Doveva essere una partita concreta e io l'ho vista: hanno giocato 90' con una certa attenzione e che ha fatto vedere anche cose buone non avendo sofferto un granché e in un momento di difficoltà ha fatto un'ottima cosa.

Non è la partita più bella che ho visto in Europa negli ultimi anni, ma è la partita che doveva giocare. Il problema più serio che ha Chivu oggi è non avere il titolare a centrocampo, Calhanoglu, la prima alternativa che è Zielinski: non si fida di Stankovic, credo che si possa dire, al momento quantomeno. Nell'affanno si faceva fatica a dare il pallone a qualcuno che potesse gestirlo bene: Sucic ha fatto una buona partita, ma non credo sia quello il suo ruolo, in prospettiva per me non può farlo. Lì ci vogliono Calhanoglu o Zielinski. Nei 10' finali con l'Atalanta si è parlato di difesa e fase difensiva, io continuo a pensare che con Calhanoglu o Zielinski non prendevi 160 ripartenze perché avevi due centrocampisti in grado di tamponare. Non esiste la squadra perfetta, l'Inter non è perfetta: sta cercando di limare i suoi problemi in una stagione stratosfericamente lunga che ti porterà ad avere altri problemi.

According to recent reports, troppi si sono abituati bene e a vedere una squadra che non sbaglia niente. Noi ragioniamo spesso come se l'Inter o altre squadre fossero da sole nell'universo: esiste anche quello che c'è attorno. Se fosse una stagione normale, tutte le prime cinque in classifica sarebbero in testa: non è una stagione normale, stanno facendo qualcosa di impressionante, la Lazio ha fatto percorso netto. Sembra sempre che se sbagli mezza partita è una tragedia, non è una tragedia: io penso che nello spogliatoio dell'Inter, le tragedie che vengono vissute fuori, nei podcast e sui giornali, i giocatori più formati, non dicono che si facciano una risata, ma hanno una corazza in grado da minimizzare certi ragionamenti che vengono fatti solo perché abbiamo necessità di riempire gli spazi.

Pio Esposito? Sta giocando divinamente. Io impazzisco sul fatto che si parli di problema quando non si parla di problema per Barcellona, Bayern e PSG: però per l'Inter avere un attaccante in più è un problema. Io penso sia una benedizione: a fine stagione io penso che avrà gli stessi minuti di Thuram, cioè tantissimi. E ti dirò di più: anche Bonny deve averne tanti. Perché non è lì a fare l'ultimo: se sta bene è forte. Io non vedo un problema".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il gruppo HBHC sostiene di aver tentato senza successo di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione calcistica.

It has been revealed that la Fifa ha confermato la sottrazione di dati interni durante un recente attacco informatico. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, Il gruppo di criminalità informatica Handsome Boy Hacking Club sostiene di aver prelevato oltre 12 GB di dati e di aver tentato, senza successo, di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La conferma è riportata dal sito specializzato in cybersecurity The Record, citato da SportMediaset. L’organizzazione calcistica, che ha sede in Svizzera, ha dichiarato che gli hacker hanno violato i suoi sistemi, ottenendo un «accesso non autorizzato a un insieme limitato di informazioni personali e aziendali».

Sources indicate that un portavoce ha affermato: «La Fifa sta collaborando strettamente con le autorità competenti, incluse le forze dell'ordine». La Fifa «condanna con la massima fermezza l'acquisizione e la pubblicazione illecite di informazioni, in particolare di dati personali. Tali azioni costituiscono una violazione grave e inaccettabile della privacy e possono avere conseguenze significative per le persone coinvolte».

L’organizzazione non ha risposto a ulteriori domande sulla natura dell’incidente. La scorsa settimana, il gruppo Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) ha dichiarato di aver sottratto oltre 12 GB di dati alla Fifa. Il gruppo ha anche riferito di aver tentato senza successo di estorcerle denaro.

Tra le informazioni sottratte figurerebbero documenti d’identità e relativi all’immigrazione, documentazione finanziaria e legale, informazioni sulla governance e altri dati.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his newly introduced kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this latest Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

In a recent development, jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

In a recent development, despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

In a recent development, mcGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Sources indicate that emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

It has been revealed that “It’s very notable to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

According to recent reports, their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

Recent findings suggest that villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s fresh goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

According to recent reports, jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

According to recent reports, don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too substantial and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

Industry observers note that in Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

It has been revealed that the Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

In a recent development, while Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant.

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson.

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn.

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

It has been revealed that mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle concern so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He noted: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a newly introduced test.”.

It has been revealed that the experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH.

Industry observers note that emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a latest-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of major-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s upcoming-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his upcoming recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Recent findings suggest that although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

L'anticipo di Galli - Da Atene torna un Milan europeo

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (992 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Milannews

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Le critiche nei confronti di Amorim rispetto al cammino rossonero in Europa League erano state impietose.
  • Nel frattempo, il tecnico portoghese è riuscito a mantenere la rotta almeno in campionato, riuscendo a dare continuità di risultati (caduta interna con il Bologna a parte) e a consolidare la posizione nella classifica della Serie A, specie dopo la sfuriata contro il Frosinone di Alvini, considerato fino a quel momento la rivelazione della stagione.
  • Insomma, fra Italia ed Europa risultati e prestazioni così differenti che sembravano appartenere a due squadre diverse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Le critiche nei confronti di Amorim rispetto al cammino rossonero in Europa League erano state impietose. Stampa e tifosi avevano sottolineato sia i presunti errori di formazione, siaun approccio alla gara non in linea con il blasone internazionale del Club. In particolare, nella prima gara casalinga con il Benfica l’accento era stato messo su un turnover eccessivo e la conseguente prestazione, mentre nelle altre due sconfitte, una a Bournemouth (un pesante 3-0) e l’altra, a San Siro contro il Ferencvaros, le accuse si erano focalizzate sulla mancanza di determinazione della squadra. In mezzo, unica nota positiva, la netta vittoria (4-0) contro il Red Bull. Un totale di quattro goal fatti, tutti nella stessa gara, e sette subiti rappresentava uno schiaffo non solo per il blasone europeo del Milan, ma anche per le aspirazioni attuali, ben più modeste. Non solo i risultati: anche le prestazioni, come ho accennato, non erano state quelle che tutti si aspettavano. E nemmeno il fatto che le tre squadre che ci avevano sconfitto occupassero, dopo quattro partite, i primi tre posti nella classifica parziale, poteva giustificare l’andamento così deludente dei rossoneri nella competizione europea.

Nel frattempo, il tecnico portoghese è riuscito a mantenere la rotta almeno in campionato, riuscendo a dare continuità di risultati (caduta interna con il Bologna a parte) e a consolidare la posizione nella classifica della Serie A, specie dopo la sfuriata contro il Frosinone di Alvini, considerato fino a quel momento la rivelazione della stagione.

Insomma, fra Italia ed Europa risultati e prestazioni così differenti che sembravano appartenere a due squadre diverse. Per questo c’era molta attesa, più di quella che un match nella fase a gironi dell’Europa League farebbe presagire, per la partita contro l’Olimpiakos. I greci, va detto, viaggiavano con un ruolino di marcia di tutto rispetto: tre vittorie e un pareggio. Avversari non irresistibili in attacco ma decisamente solidi in difesa(sette goal subiti nelle undici partite di campionato e soltanto uno nelle quattro di Europa League). Tutto, compresa l’atmosfera che i nostri ragazzi avrebbero trovato allo stadio Karaiskakis, tradizionalmente incandescente, lasciava presagire un’altra serata difficile per Amorim e i suoi ragazzi.

Sources indicate that E così è stato, in particolare nel primo tempo. Un inizio da brividi, come da recente abitudine, con due goal subiti. Poi Omari Hutchinson, inizialmente costretto in una posizione da trequartista centrale, si è spostato a destra; ma, soprattutto, ha deciso di accendere la luce e di svegliare i compagni, che evidentemente si erano assopiti. Al minuto 56 l’anglo-giamaicano ha preso la palla a ridosso della nostra area, ha percorso quasi tutto il campo, si è accentrato da destra verso sinistra e ha lasciato partire un sinistro che si è infilato nell’angolino: da lì è partita la reazione del Milan che, grazie a due assist dello stesso Hutchinson (uno di destro e uno di sinistro, per gradire), ha portato dapprima al pareggio (Cisse) e poi addirittura al vantaggio (Pulisic), sigillato da Diego Moreira.

In a recent development, È questa reazione a farmi pensare che i rossoneri siano nel pieno di un processo per diventare squadra. Un processo che passa necessariamente dalla consapevolezza deipropri punti di forza, ma anche dei propri margini di miglioramento (ci torneremo).

Nel Milan odierno ogni giocatore si mette a disposizione del proprio compagno. Nessuno, neppure lo stesso Modric, spesso portato ad esempio e giustamente considerato il leader in campo e nello spogliatoio, si sente protagonista assoluto. Tutti concorrono a realizzare l’idea di gioco e il piano gara del tecnico Amorim. Prova ne sia la partita con il Frosinone,in cui il Milan ha rinunciato all’idea di fare la partita nella metà campo avversaria e ha assecondato la tendenza dei ciociari ad andare uomo su uomo già nella fase della nostra prima costruzione di gioco, per poi trafiggerli ripetutamente in transizione. Questa capacità di adattarsi all’avversario rappresenta secondo me un’importante prova di avvenuta maturazione di Amorim e della squadra, specie se la si confronta con la già menzionatadebacle casalinga contro il Bologna.

Anche se non mi piace mai cercare un capro espiatorio, mi sembra utile inserire nell’equazione Rafa Leao: nel recente passato, si tendeva a pensare che il talentuoso portoghese, con le sue doti tecniche e atletiche, avrebbe prima o poi risolto la partita con uno dei suoi strappi, che ci hanno regalato uno scudetto, ma che negli ultimi anni erano diventati sempre più rari. In questo modo gli altri giocatori tendevano a deresponsabilizzarsi e a non esprimere tutto il loro potenziale. Il Milan di oggi può contare su un gruppo di giocatori offensivi di buon livello (buono o ottimo? Lo capiremo), ma soprattutto su una migliore distribuzione delle responsabilità in campo.

Industry observers note that C’è tanto da migliorare. In particolare, come già detto negli editoriali precedenti e come lo stesso Amorim ha ammesso nella conferenza stampa del post gara, la squadra deve migliorare l’attenzione difensiva, sui calci piazzati in cui regolarmente concediamo troppo agli avversari, e non solo. E preoccupa il fatto che gli errori si ripetano anche quando cambiano gli interpreti: ieri, ad esempio, De Winter è apparso molto stanco, forse più mentalmente che fisicamente.

Però i segnali positivi ci sono: come abbiamo detto, in questo Milan tutti, anche i più giovani, si assumono le proprie responsabilità. Il processo di crescita è costellato di errori e l’essere squadra significa anche rimediare senza colpevolizzare nessuno, qualsiasi sia l’esito della gara. A turno, Cisse, Moreira, Pulisic, Rabiot, Ramos, e persino Jashari hanno lasciato il segno. Ieri sera è stato il turno di Hutchinson, con una serata europea che non dimenticherà facilmente. Come una combo jazz, nella quale ogni solista sa quando prendere il centro del palco, ma anche quando mettersi al servizio del compagno.

In a recent development, ora l’Europa ha tutta un’altra faccia, e le tre partite che mancano sono abbordabili. In compenso lunedì ci aspetta l’insidiosa trasferta di Cagliari, una tappa che ci darà ulteriori risposte. Non c’è il tempo di compiacersi, i progressi vanno confermati ogni volta.

Il Corriere della Sera scrive del momento del Napoli, reduce dal pareggio in Champions a Manchester contro il City: “Ha scelto la notte di Manchester, Allegri, per inseguire qualcosa di speciale. E ha sfiorato il grande colpo. Avanti 2-1 fino a 4 minuti dalla fine, il Napoli (sopra tutti Milinkovic) si è arreso al diagonale avvelenato di Cherki e il City ha agguantato il pari togliendo al Napoli due punti che l’avrebbero rilanciato in Champions. Resta il 2-2 sul campo di una delle grandi potenze d’Europa. Un 2-2 che gli azzurri hanno meritato per aver disinnescato il giro palla e abbattuto la creatività del City, senza mai rinunciare a ripartire. Le incursioni di McTominay, l’orgoglio di De Bruyne in uno stadio che ancora lo adora, i cross affilati di Politano, la rapidità di Lang e la guardia attenta su Haaland: il Napoli ha giocato con personalità, concentrazione e attenzione. Il palleggio del City lo ha scalfito ma non è riuscito a scardinare la sua organizzazione. Spazi occupati e reattività alla base della guerriglia organizzata da Allegri, che esce da Manchester con un’ottima notizia: la squadra lo segue, è dalla sua parte”.

  • There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars.

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham.

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’.

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’.

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

England manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team.

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America.

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’.

Prima compagni e poi allenatore e giocatore, ora Gattuso e Abate si sfidano nelle rispettive aree tecniche.

Sabato pomeriggio Torino-Lazio vedrà Gennaro Gattuso e Ignazio Abate uno contro l’altro uno contro l'altro da allenatori, con i biancocelesti concentrata sul proprio percorso e i granata la cui ultima vittoria in campionato risale ormai a un mese fa. Un incrocio che riporta indietro nel tempo, al loro lungo passato condiviso al Milan prima sul campo e poi in panchina.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il loro primo incontro risale all’estate del 2009, quando Abate tornò al Milan ritrovando Gattuso già senatore del gruppo. Fino al 2012 hanno condiviso spogliatoio e campo, vincendo insieme lo Scudetto 2010-2011 e la Supercoppa Italiana, con Gattuso punto di riferimento per la crescita del compagno.

Recent findings suggest that nel novembre 2017 si sono ritrovati con Gattuso passato sulla panchina del Milan, dove si è ritrovato ad allenare un Abate ancora in campo e ormai veterano. Il rapporto è rimasto schietto e diretto, con Gattuso che ha chiesto sempre il massimo fino a schierarlo anche da difensore centrale in emergenza, prima del comune addio al club nel maggio 2019.

Fabio Ravezzani, giornalista, si è così espresso sul suo canale Youtube commentando la vittoria del Milan contro l'Olympiacos: "Vincono il Milan e la Juventus in Europa League, due partite piene di chiaroscuri che finiscono in gloria, che danno un rilancio importante del calcio italiano. Vi ricordo che dopo due turni di Champions e di Europa League eravamo tutti a piangere: «siamo un calcio di Serie B, no di Serie C», invece adesso tutte le nostre squadre vincono o pareggiano, dimostrazione che non siamo poi così malmessi, come ogni tanto ci piace raccontare e piangerci un po' addosso. Allora, due partite in cui nei primi tempi ci sarebbe semplicemente da disperarsi. Il Milan e la Juventus hanno giocato non male, peggio, con un aggravante per la Juventus perché giocare in casa contro l'Omonia Nicosia è ben diverso che giocare contro l'Olympiakos ad Atene, però anche qui il Milan è stato inguardabile ed è successo un fatto abbastanza bizzarro che mi pare Amorim non abbia colto fino in fondo".

Ravezzani entra poi nel dettaglio: "Amorim dice: «come siamo stati bravi, queste sono partite che cambiano una stagione, abbiamo conquistato l'autostima»; passare da -2 a 0 a +4 o 2 è un grande momento anche di riscatto, di catarsi della squadra e ha ragione, è esattamente così. Però si dimentica di un fatto Amorim, e cioè che il Milan è risorto e rifiorito nel momento in cui è uscito Gonçalo Ramos, è entrato Cisse e si è messo a fare l'attaccante. Cisse ha fatto quelle cose che tutti si aspettano da Gonçalo Ramos e che non accadono mai. Ora io lo so bene quello che molti di voi pensano e stanno pensando in questo momento: «sì, però Gonçalo Ramos fa un lavoro oscuro importante per la squadra perché si sacrifica»; tutto vero, è straordinario il lavoro che fa Gonçalo Ramos, ma in una squadra c'è chi si sacrifica e c'è chi pensa invece a finalizzare, a fare gol. Ora si possono trovare le giuste contromisure in maniera tale che la squadra nella sua totalità riesca a fare un buon pressing senza che un attaccante debba per forza di cose massacrarsi, salvo poi al momento di fare il suo mestiere non avere la lucidità o non avere, diciamo la verità, i numeri.".

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
