⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Industry observers note that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a newly introduced manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Sources indicate that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

It has been revealed that playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

Sources indicate that there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

In a recent development, newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Industry observers note that well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil mentioned: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

Sources indicate that “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

Industry observers note that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

Recent findings suggest that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

Recent findings suggest that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” said Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is vital], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a newly introduced coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a major game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We said at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Industry observers note that willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

According to recent reports, finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Sources indicate that marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Recent findings suggest that issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

According to recent reports, millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Recent findings suggest that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

According to recent reports, what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

Sources indicate that it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

It has been revealed that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Recent findings suggest that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

It has been revealed that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Recent findings suggest that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Industry observers note that newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

In a recent development, gonzález is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Sources indicate that millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Recent findings suggest that hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

According to recent reports, first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Sources indicate that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Industry observers note that wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Sources indicate that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Industry observers note that again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

According to recent reports, murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

It has been revealed that fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Sources indicate that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Recent findings suggest that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach claims has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

Recent findings suggest that the Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Recent findings suggest that bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

Per festeggiare il Natale, quest'anno la Lazio ha pensato ad un evento differente rispetto alla consueta cena.

Per festeggiare il Natale, quest'anno la Lazio ha pensato ad un evento differente rispetto alla consueta cena, che si svolgeva di solito a Spazio Novecento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that come si legge dal comunicato della Lazio con la lettera di Lotito riportata dal Corriere dello Sport, quest'anno l'invito per i tesserati della Lazio è per sabato 19 dicembre alle 15.00 per celebrare la messa di Natale. Inoltre verranno destinate risorse al sostegno di alcune realtà della nostra città che ogni giorno si impegnano ad aiutare le persone e le famiglie che vivono situazioni di difficoltà”.

A tutti i tesserati, dipendenti e collaboratori della S.S. Lazio.

il Natale è soprattutto un momento per stare insieme, ritrovarsi e ricordare ciò che conta davvero.

Quest’anno abbiamo pensato di scambiarci gli auguri in un modo diverso, più semplice, ma forse proprio per questo ancora più significativo.

Recent findings suggest that sabato 19 dicembre 2026, alle ore 15:00, ci ritroveremo nella parrocchia San Tommaso Moro, di Don Gabriele, nel quartiere San Lorenzo a Roma, per celebrare insieme la Santa Messa di Natale. Vorrei che fosse un momento per tutti noi, per sentirci parte di una comunità che ogni giorno condivide lavoro, impegno, responsabilità, gioie e difficoltà. Perché la Lazio, prima ancora di essere una società sportiva, è fatta di persone.

Quest’anno abbiamo anche deciso di vivere lo spirito del Natale attraverso un gesto concreto di solidarietà, destinando risorse al sostegno di alcune realtà della nostra città che ogni giorno si impegnano ad aiutare le persone e le famiglie che vivono situazioni di difficoltà.

Ci sono tante persone e tante famiglie che stanno attraversando momenti complicati. Credo che il modo migliore per vivere lo spirito del Natale sia anche quello di pensare a loro, rinunciando a qualcosa per noi per poter offrire qualcosa agli altri.

Non sarà un gesto che risolverà tutti i problemi, ma sarà il nostro modo di esserci, concretamente.

Industry observers note that mi piacerebbe davvero che il 19 dicembre fossimo tutti presenti. Non per un appuntamento formale, ma per il piacere di ritrovarci, guardarci negli occhi, scambiarci gli auguri e condividere un momento che appartiene a tutti noi.

Perché essere una comunità significa anche questo: sentirsi parte di qualcosa e sapere che, insieme, possiamo fare del bene.

Vi aspetto e, fin da ora, auguro a voi e alle vostre famiglie un Natale sereno, con l’auspicio che il nuovo anno possa portare salute, pace e soddisfazioni.

Claudio Lotito Presidente S.S. Lazio.

Parrocchia San Tommaso Moro Via dei Ramni, 40, 00185 Roma (angolo Via dei Marrucini).

Enrico Preziosi torna a parlare. Il vulcanico ex presidente del Genoa lo ha fatto ai microfoni della Gazzetta dello Sport alla vigilia della gara tra il Grifone e l'Inter, ricordando alcuni aneddoti legati anche alla figura di Massimo Moratti: “Con lui ho sempre avuto un rapporto di grande cordialità: un gentiluomo con cui trattare era un piacere anche perché poi si arrendeva sempre, una persona perbene, non speculava mai. Però mi deve ancora 5 milioni di euro…”.

Industry observers note that “Milito e Thiago Motta hanno fatto vincere il Triplete all’Inter! Quell’anno Moratti ed io facemmo una scommessa: lui ripeteva che per il Principe ‘giocare a Milano non sarebbe stato come a Genova’ e che sarebbe stato difficile che raggiungesse anche solo 10 gol. Gli risposi che se ne avesse fatti una dozzina mi avrebbe pagato altri 5 milioni… e ne segnò 30. Lui accettò, però poi non ne parlammo più. Un giorno sistemeremo i conti”.

M&M’s, Milito e Motta, la fortuna dell’Inter. Ma non l’unico affare tra Genoa ed Inter.

“Nella stessa operazione c’erano pure Bonucci e Ranocchia. Gasperini mi ha sempre rimproverato le loro cessioni, era molto arrabbiato con me perché già all’epoca li considerava due difensori importanti. Ne discutemmo parecchio, anche vivacemente. Gli attaccai il telefono in faccia ma poi ci abbracciammo. C’era troppa stima reciproca per tenersi il muso, ancora oggi mi manda le vecchie fotografie dei derby, del 3-1 con tripletta di Milito, abbiamo un bel rapporto. E oggi sta facendo un campionato straordinario, con una squadra non tanto completa per giustificare questi meravigliosi risultati. La sua mano si vede sempre”.

La delusione più grande acquistata dai nerazzurri?

“Il terzo dentro quel maxi-affare: Acquafresca. Più che altro, Acqua-tiepidina… Valutato un’esagerazione, aveva segnato un sacco di gol ma poi aveva smesso all’improvviso. Da noi non si è mai espresso a livelli accettabili, anzi credo si sia ritirato abbastanza presto. Si starà godendo i nostri soldi da qualche parte”.

“No, proprio no. Come Zé Eduardo, lì, Zé Love… Ero andato in Brasile per comprare Neymar e sono tornato con quell’altro. Avevano lo stesso procuratore che mi disse ‘Guarda, ho una stella meravigliosa, meglio di O’Ney’. Forse l’aveva già venduto al Barcellona e alla fine mi convinse”.

Zé Love, quello del famoso provino al Milan.

“Una tragedia. Allegri lo mandò via subito”.

Ma che storia è quella di Neymar al Genoa?

Recent findings suggest that “Andai in Brasile perché avevo un appuntamento con il suo procuratore per portarlo in Italia. C’era anche Galliani, con cui all’epoca discutevo di Boateng che poi sarebbe andato al Milan perché a Gasperini non piaceva. Adriano è un amico: decidemmo di partire per questi dieci giorni in Brasile in cui tra l’altro beccammo solo pioggia”.

Pensa che il Genoa possa fare uno scherzetto all’Inter tra campionato e Coppa Italia?

Industry observers note that “Nel calcio sappiamo che ogni tanto avvengono dei miracoli o comunque delle cose strane, ma non credo. L’Inter è chiaramente più forte e penso che sarà molto difficile che perda a San Siro. Anche in Coppa Italia, perché è un trofeo che interessa alle grandi squadre. Poi, se succede il miracolo, ben venga. Sarei molto felice per il Genoa”.

It has been revealed that in casa Napoli c’è ottimismo dopo il buon risultato a Manchester, un pari che regala buone sensazioni in vista delle prossime gare. Uno dei migliori in questo periodo è Scott McTominay e ieri nel prepartita del match il Ds Giovanni Manna ha incontrato a Manchester l’agente del giocatore e si è parlato del rinnovo.

Industry observers note that come riporta il Corriere dello Sport il club ha manifestato al giocatore l’intenzione di rinnovare il contratto, lo scozzese è fondamentale e anche in queste ultime gare ha dimostrato la sua importanza nella squadra di Allegri. Ma il procuratore del calciatore ha manifestato a Manna e alla società l’intenzione di veder riconosciuta quest’importanza.

In a recent development, come riporta il Corriere dello Sport Scott McTominay vuole ben 10 milioni di euro all’anno, un ultimo grande contratto che lo determini come uomo chiave all’interno del club, fondamentale anche in chiave futura. Il Napoli vuole accontentare il giocatore, ma ovviamente bisognerà trovare un punto di incontro.

Gli addii di Anguissa e De Bruyne a fine stagione potrebbero facilitare, ma occorre trovare un’intesa e non sarà semplice. Il quotidiano parla di inverno piuttosto freddo e intenso nelle dinamiche del club partenopeo.

  • Recent findings suggest that È stato Hutchinson a cambare la partita: "La sua fuga, sulla destra, è stata - ha raccontato Guadagno - come una scossa elettrica per tutto il Milan.

Pietro Guadagno, giornalista, si è così espresso sul Corriere dello Sport commentando la vittoria del Milan per 2-4 sull'Olympiacos: "Da un’altra figuraccia sfiorata al ribaltone. In casa dell’Olympiacos, per 50’, il Milan ha mostrato il peggio di sé, come era già accaduto, sempre in Europa League, anche contro Benfica, Bournemouth e Ferencvaros. Incassati 2 gol, si stava già manifestando lo spettro di una clamorosa eliminazione dalla prima fase. Improvvisamente, invece, si è accesa la luce di Hutchinson ed è sbocciato un Diavolo completamente diverso: intenso, aggressivo, finalmente attento e coperto dietro. I greci, scomparsi letteralmente dal campo, sono rimasti annichiliti, incassando, nello spazio di un quarto d’ora, 3 reti: tutte ispirate dal funambolico inglese".

Recent findings suggest that È stato Hutchinson a cambare la partita: "La sua fuga, sulla destra, è stata - ha raccontato Guadagno - come una scossa elettrica per tutto il Milan. Ha bruciato due avversari, si è accentrato, ha preso la mira e, dal limite, ha infilzato Ortega sul palo lontano. Si è capito subito che la partita era cambiata. E la marea rossonera ha cominciato a montare. Hutchinson ha imperversato sulla fascia destra, catapultando in area palloni che erano cioccolatini solo da scartare. Sul primo si è avventato Cisse, che, abbandonato da Retsos, di testa ha superato un impacciato Ortega: 4° centro europeo per lui e 10° in stagione. Sul secondo, Pulisic, tutto solo in mezzo all’area, si è esibito in una semirovesciata al volo che ha sancito il sorpasso. A sigillare la vittoria, nel recupero, ci ha pensato Moreira, finalizzando un contropiede su imbeccata dell’ex Chelsea, che poco prima aveva sprecato una ripartenza in 4 contro uno".

Il commentatore apprezza anche Taylor e Nuno Tavares, prima di confrontare Roma e Inter nella corsa in campionato.

Sources indicate that bruno Longhi elogia la Lazio per il suo gioco e per la disposizione dei calciatori in campo. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Intervenuto a Maracanà sui temi della Serie A, ha detto: «Attenzione però che io sono innamorato della Lazio, la vedo giocare ed è uno spettacolo. Ha i giocatori giusti al posto giusto. Non la metterei in disparte.».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Longhi ha poi indicato alcuni dei giocatori che apprezza nella squadra biancoceleste: «La Lazio ha tutti giocatori che mi piacciono. Isaksen mi ricorda Robben, poi Taylor, Nuno Tavares, una squadra dove tutti giocano bene ed è un piacere vederla». Il paragone con Robben riguarda dunque Isaksen, mentre il giudizio positivo si estende al gioco dell’intera squadra.

Parlando della Roma, Longhi ha definito inatteso il segnale arrivato dalla squadra. Ha richiamato City-Napoli, partita in cui a suo giudizio aveva prevalso il tatticismo, e l’ha contrapposta alla gara giocata a viso aperto sul campo del PSG, che nelle sue parole domina da due anni in Champions. La Roma, ha osservato, ha affrontato l’impegno come se avesse davanti un’altra squadra di Serie A.

Recent findings suggest that longhi ha descritto la formazione giallorossa attraverso forza, temperamento, pressing e tecnica. Di Gasperini ha detto che ha giocato sul campo del PSG scegliendo i calciatori da impiegare senza preoccupazioni: per lui è il segnale di una rosa adatta a qualsiasi tipo di impegno.

Sources indicate that sull’Inter il giudizio è diverso: «Ha disputato 17 partite e non si è mai vista l'Inter come lo scorso anno o di due anni fa, per vari motivi. L'Inter rimane forte, però rimane indecifrabile.» Per questo, nel confronto di campionato, Longhi indica più la Roma dei nerazzurri.

Industry observers note that in vista del derby di domenica prossima, il tecnico del Liverpool Andoni Iraola ha fatto il punto della situazione sugli infortuni: "Gakpo sicuramente non ci sarà. Si tratta di un infortunio muscolare, quindi dobbiamo attendere che il processo di guarigione faccia il suo corso. Per quanto riguarda Victor, la buona notizia è che, dopo gli accertamenti, non sono emersi danni al ginocchio; è tutto a posto. Tuttavia, ha subito una brutta botta. Oggi non si è allenato, ma vuole provare a farlo domani. Vedremo come evolve l'ematoma, ma al momento non posso dare certezze.

It has been revealed that per un infortunio come quello di Gakpo, solitamente sono necessarie due o tre settimane. Se l'è procurato nell'ultima partita con i Paesi Bassi contro la Germania, quindi i tempi sono più o meno questi. In genere, però, preferisco non sbilanciarmi sulle tempistiche, perché ogni infortunio è diverso e alcuni richiedono tempi di recupero più brevi di altri.

It has been revealed that non è un infortunio grave, ma c'è comunque un problema che richiede il giusto tempo per guarire. Gravenberch? Sarà difficile. Non voglio escludere nulla a priori, ma questo tipo di infortuni è complesso. A volte non sembrano nulla di grave, eppure il dolore persiste. A volte la situazione migliora, senza un motivo apparente, per poi peggiorare di nuovo il giorno successivo. Lui sta affrontando questa situazione e noi cerchiamo di aiutarlo. La cosa fondamentale è che, al suo rientro, non avverta più alcun dolore, così da poter giocare con la massima libertà possibile".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’emendamento di Pella richiede una valutazione motivata della convenienza dell’accordo rispetto a una nuova gara.

Un emendamento alla manovra propone di prorogare di due anni, fino al 2031, l’attuale contratto dei diritti tv della Serie A, in scadenza nel 2029. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Fatto Quotidiano, La proposta è firmata da Roberto Pella, esponente di Forza Italia e collega di partito di Claudio Lotito, senatore e presidente della Lazio. L’emendamento figura tra i 700 emendamenti «s e gn a l ati » alla manovra in Parlamento, .

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La proposta porta in Parlamento l’ipotesi di mantenere più a lungo gli accordi attuali con gli operatori. Arriva dopo mesi di contatti condotti sotto traccia, con l’idea di tentare un intervento parlamentare.

According to recent reports, I diritti tv valgono poco meno di un miliardo di euro e sostengono il calcio italiano. Dal 2021 la quota maggiore, circa 700 milioni di euro, è garantita da Dazn, mentre Sky ha un ruolo secondario. La scadenza del contratto nel 2029 preoccupa i presidenti dei club: il mercato dei campionati nazionali è in flessione a livello mondiale, anche per la concorrenza della Champions League, ed è debole in Italia.

Sources indicate that in assenza di concorrenza, le offerte tendono a diminuire. Secondo la ricostruzione, i presidenti temono un forte calo degli introiti anche perché ritengono che il prodotto non valga la spesa richiesta agli operatori.

La Lega Serie A si è già mossa in vista della scadenza. L’Antitrust ha approvato le linee guida e il bando per il periodo 2029-2034 è atteso a inizio anno. L’amministratore delegato Luigi De Siervo, indicato come vicino alla conclusione del proprio percorso, è riuscito in passato a trovare soluzioni per i diritti tv: la prossima assegnazione resta il passaggio da affrontare.

Recent findings suggest that un’alternativa alla vendita dei diritti è il canale della Serie A, progetto per il quale la Lega si sta strutturando come media company. L’esperienza francese, descritta come fallimentare, e le difficoltà della stessa Dazn mostrano però quanto sia complicato ottenere dagli abbonamenti le risorse necessarie a far quadrare i conti.

La proroga rappresenterebbe una terza strada: mantenere per altri due anni gli accordi alle stesse cifre sarebbe vantaggioso per la Serie A. Per i broadcaster, in teoria, potrebbe esserci maggiore interesse a partecipare a una nuova gara. Dazn, tuttavia, punta alla quotazione in Borsa e ha interesse ad arrivarci con contratti importanti, come quello della Serie A, senza affrontare l’incertezza del bando. Sky, dal canto suo, ha trovato un proprio equilibrio.

Quanto ai tifosi, la ricostruzione attribuisce a una parte di loro una forte ostilità verso Dazn, giudicata in parte immotivata. Ricorda però anche i disservizi iniziali e le oscillazioni delle tariffe della piattaforma.

According to recent reports, sulle pagine odierne della Gazzetta dello Sport, Alessandro Vocalelli ha parlato così di Omari Hutchinson, grande protagonista ieri sera della vittoria del Milan contro l'Olympiacos con un gol e due assist: "Di sicuro i tifosi milanisti hanno vissuto ieri sera una bellissima serata, in una sorta di roulette – rossonera – nel giro di poco più di mezz’ora. Al 55’ i greci comandavano infatti per due a zero e, anche se nessuno lo confesserà, le critiche stavano già montando nei confronti di Amorim; poi, però, lo scenario è radicalmente cambiato. Anche – anzi, soprattutto – perché sul palcoscenico si è presentato un ragazzo inglese, che di sicuro non ama passare inosservato e non solo per quel doppio taglio che si accende di biondo nella parte superiore. Sì, perché Hutchinson adora farsi notare anche per il suo calcio spregiudicato, apparentemente effervescente ma in realtà concreto. Il gol che ha spianato la strada alla rimonta è stato infatti un concentrato di esplosività, forza, velocità, intelligenza, precisione e lucidità: non è affatto facile piazzare il pallone in buca d’angolo dopo aver percorso sessanta metri a perdifiato.

In a recent development, ora di inglesi nel nostro campionato hanno cominciato ad arrivarne tanti, ma una volta capitava molto più raramente e – si può dire? – erano forse più le delusioni che le scommesse vinte. Lui, con le dovute proporzioni in un calcio che cambia ogni stagione come le mode, ha qualcosa nelle movenze che ricorda il connazionale David Platt. Ed è un grande complimento. Fatto sta che, dopo Gila, Moreira e Ramos, sarà il caso di aggiungere anche lui (in attesa dei rinforzi di gennaio) alla lista degli acquisti concepiti da Cardinale per puntare in alto".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

Industry observers note that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a latest City, different personnel and even a new look.

It has been revealed that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

In a recent development, “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are latest to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

According to recent reports, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This highlights how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he revealed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

According to recent reports, “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland remarked. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the major stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Industry observers note that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

It has been revealed that “I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Recent findings suggest that “We are going to face one of the substantial favourites to win the competition,” Farioli mentioned. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Industry observers note that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISAAN KHAN, REPORTER and WILL GRIFFEE.

Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mikel Arteta noted David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Recent findings suggest that raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ said Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle.

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’.

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’.

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright noted on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

Industry observers note that 'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'.

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes stated Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened.

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ said the Brazilian.

It has been revealed that ‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

‘He indicated me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’.

Arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a newly introduced innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

According to recent reports, progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop new features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' said Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

According to recent reports, 'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'.

Sources indicate that the feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

It has been revealed that michael Cuomo, giornalista, si è così espresso sul canale Youtube di Carlos Passerini commentando la partita di Omari Hutchinson: "Stavo seguendo la partita ovviamente su Sky in telecronaca, Marchegiani dice una cosa che ho pensato subito anch'io: non è tanto il gol che fa, ma è come lo fa. C'è quella cavalcata da cavallo pazzo che fa, non lo abbatti, hanno tentato di abbatterlo e non ci sono riusciti. E poi quel tiro all'angolino alla destra del portiere: Marchegiani dice subito che non è importante soltanto perché riapre la partita, ma perché dà anche una scarica emotiva, un po' di leggerezza a questa squadra che era un po' in bambola in quel momento. E io dentro di me stavo pensando la stessa identica cosa: quando ho sentito Marchegiani dire questa frase ho detto «io l'ho pensata e lui l'ha detta». E Hucthinson poi non solo dà una scarica con quel gol bellissimo, ma fa anche gli assist".

"Era - ribadisce Cuomo - una questione di testa: il gol di Hutchinson stappa un po' mentalmente questa squadra. Alla fine era una questione mentale, nel senso che poi, infatti, al 2-0 io dico: «ma scusami, proviamo a paragonare l'Olympiakos, lo paragoniamo a questa Atalanta?» e tu mi dici «un po' meno». E allora io dico: «com'è possibile che si vada così in bambola e che si sia così...». Io obiettivamente Pirola l'ho conosciuto, stiamo parlando di uno che era riuscito quasi a fare doppietta di testa e di piede. Ma quello che dico è che è evidente che sia un problema di testa, perché poi, quando la partita si è rimessa su un binario credibile, su un binario favorevole, sembrava che le gambe girassero di più, girassero meglio".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Per l’ex compagno, i due tecnici hanno idee chiare; la Lazio attacca con molti uomini, mentre il Toro cerca stabilità.

Massimo Ambrosini presenta Torino-Lazio come la prima sfida in panchina tra i suoi ex compagni Ignazio Abate e Rino Gattuso. Secondo quanto riportato da La Stampa, La partita del 28 novembre 2026, allo stadio Grande Torino, mette di fronte i granata in cerca di rivincita e i biancocelesti, primi in classifica e ancora imbattuti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, ripensando al Milan dello scudetto 2010/11, Ambrosini racconta che si aspettava di vedere Gattuso allenatore, mentre Abate lo aveva sorpreso per la curiosità e l’applicazione mostrate nello studio del gioco: «Ero quasi sicuro che Rino sarebbe diventato un allenatore, Ignazio un po’ meno. È sempre stato un grande entusiasta e una persona positiva, ma non lo facevo così curioso e applicato dal punto di vista teorico». Di quella squadra sono diventati tecnici anche Nesta, Inzaghi, Seedorf, Oddo e Pirlo.

Industry observers note that commentatore di Dazn, che trasmetterà l’incontro, Ambrosini si aspetta una prova coraggiosa dal Torino. Giocando in casa, i granata possono cercare una svolta senza lasciarsi intimidire dalla capolista. La Lazio, invece, dovrebbe continuare ad attaccare con molti uomini, senza modificare la propria idea di gioco in base all’avversario.

Recent findings suggest that «Il Toro deve fare una partita coraggiosa perché gioca in casa e può dare una svolta, quindi mi aspetto una prova gagliarda da parte di una squadra che non si spaventerà di affrontare la capolista. La Lazio, invece, giocherà come sempre: vorrà fare la partita, attaccando con tanti uomini. Rino ha già fatto vedere che cambiano gli avversari, ma non la sua idea di calcio», dice Ambrosini.

Quanto a una possibile carriera personale in panchina, la risposta dell’ex centrocampista è netta e scherzosa: «No, non mi avranno mai (ride, ndr). Sto bene così».

Industry observers note that per Ambrosini, il primato della Lazio si lega alle capacità di Gattuso e al lavoro svolto su una base già solida. L’ex capitano rossonero ricorda il calcio espresso dalle squadre allenate da Rino al Milan e al Napoli, distinguendo da quelle esperienze la parentesi in Nazionale, che considera particolare anche per i giocatori a disposizione.

According to recent reports, «Rino lo conosco bene e conosco la capacità che ha di far giocare le proprie squadre. Al di là della Nazionale, una parentesi molto particolare anche per gli uomini che aveva a disposizione, Milan e Napoli giocavano un bel calcio con lui. È la sua storia che lo racconta e se la gente ha la memoria corta... Poi da lì a pensare che una squadra nella situazione in cui era la Lazio, con tutto quello che gli gira intorno, potesse fare questo tipo di percorso... Non se lo aspettava neanche lui, ma è giusto che sia primo per quel che sta facendo in campo», osserva Ambrosini.

It has been revealed that alla base del rendimento biancoceleste indica l’empatia costruita dal tecnico e i principi di gioco: «C’era una base solida, ma l’empatia creata da Gattuso e i principi di gioco hanno fatto la differenza». Il lavoro sulla fiducia, secondo Ambrosini, ha inciso anche sulla crescita dei singoli.

Industry observers note that «La testa è fondamentale, ma non basta. Gattuso ha saputo tirare fuori il meglio da Isaksen, Frattesi o Taylor perché ha dato le conoscenze giuste per farli sentire in fiducia: così riesci a sfruttare il potenziale tecnico e atletico di ognuno», spiega.

According to recent reports, il 28 novembre 1982, al Cino e Lillo Del Duca di Ascoli si presenta una Juventus stellare. Campioni come Paolo Rossi, Platini, Tardelli, Scirea e Boniek sfidano i bianconeri marchigiani per l’undicesima giornata di campionato. La Juve nell’ultimo mese ha inanellato una serie di prestazioni convincenti, culminate con il successo nel derby contro il Torino, deciso ancora una volta da una giocata di Le Roi Platini.

Il momento attraversato dall’Ascoli è di altro tenore. La squadra di Mazzone ha raccolto pochi punti, ma tra i tifosi del Picchio c’è ancora spazio per la speranza. I marchigiani crescono con il passare dei minuti e al 25’ trovano il meritato vantaggio. Novellino riesce a controllare il pallone tra due avversari, addomesticandolo con il petto prima di scaricare un mancino verso la porta. La conclusione non sembra particolarmente insidiosa, ma la grande densità di giocatori davanti a Zoff finisce per ostacolare la visuale del portiere, che non riesce a intervenire.

In a recent development, poi, quando il primo tempo sta per concludersi, arriva anche il colpo del definitivo ko. Sugli sviluppi di una punizione dal limite, il pallone finisce nuovamente tra i piedi di Novellino: conclusione straordinaria, un gesto tecnico a metà tra il pallonetto e il tiro a giro, indirizzato verso il secondo palo. Zoff è nuovamente battuto. È il 2-0 con cui terminerà la gara.

Marcatori: Novellino 25, Novellino 45.

ASCOLI Brini, Anzivino, Boldini, Menichini, Gasparini, Nicolini, Novellino, De Vecchi, Pircher (89' Muraro), Greco (76' Carotti), Monelli. Allenatore: Mazzone.

According to recent reports, JUVENTUS Zoff, Gentile, Prandelli, Furino, Brio, Scirea (46' Bonini), Bettega, Tardelli, Rossi P., Platini, Boniek. Allenatore: Trapattoni.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a significant reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

Industry observers note that ‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season.

It has been revealed that ‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

According to recent reports, ‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’.

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

It has been revealed that ‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I stated after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

According to recent reports, ‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always mentioned, and that’s been really disappointing.’.

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal.

According to recent reports, delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be major for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

Industry observers note that ‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’.
