Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face mentioned it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

It has been revealed that there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he revealed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ upcoming head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola stated, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Industry observers note that liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo highlighted he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

In a recent development, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

Industry observers note that this is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

Industry observers note that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

Recent findings suggest that there is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

In a recent development, liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

It has been revealed that atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Industry observers note that isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Industry observers note that liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

Industry observers note that we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

Recent findings suggest that the Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed newly introduced contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

Industry observers note that “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

It has been revealed that “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Recent findings suggest that when Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

In a recent development, “This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what significant clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very vital.”.

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

According to recent reports, “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola stated. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Recent findings suggest that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a significant responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid at the moment sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

It has been revealed that “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

  • There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Recent findings suggest that potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

Sources indicate that ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

Recent findings suggest that ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts claims. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

Sources indicate that ‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

It has been revealed that potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In a recent development, in Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

Industry observers note that he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

In a recent development, ‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

Potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his newly introduced surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

Recent findings suggest that he has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

In a recent development, ‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5351 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
  • Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

It has been revealed that in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

Sources indicate that “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” remarked Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

Industry observers note that in the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Sources indicate that their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

According to recent reports, “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” stated Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

Sources indicate that there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

Recent findings suggest that A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

In a recent development, throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Industry observers note that despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In a recent development, in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” stated Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

Industry observers note that “He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with latest arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:.

Touches in opposition box: 9-52.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Sempre Con Te è intervenuto Enzo Bucchioni: “Un voto alto per il Napoli, la miglior partita stagionale. Lo aspettavamo così dall’inizio. Una prestazione inattesa, finalmente però si è ritrovato l’orgoglio di una grande squadra. Si era visto in stagione qualche sprazzo di Napoli convincente. Il pareggio con il City ha un sapore differente. Non era atteso, può essere questa la ripartenza vera? C’è da augurarsi di sì. Le prossime sono alla portata. Il Napoli deve segnare di più e subire di meno? Secondo me subire di meno. È mancato il sacrificio degli attaccanti. Se non danno una mano per primi, qualsiasi fase difensiva va in difficoltà. È uscito Lang, la fase difensiva non la faceva, era pigro. Quando perdi palla devi andare con determinazione sul pallone ed è successo. La fase difensiva non funzionava per questo. Le squadre di Allegri hanno sempre avuto queste caratteristiche, ma non riusciva a farsi capire. Come vedo le parole di Allegri su De Bruyne? La posizione di De Bruyne la sappiamo, gli piace un altro calcio. Spero che contro il City si sia divertito, penso che ci sia stato anche un confronto. Un allenatore che si sbilancia lo vedo come segnale importante. Allegri ha ripreso la barca, quel tipo di calcio con il baricentro basso e rincorse all’indietro non faccia parte del bagaglio di molti giocatori. Anche Allegri ha provato a fare altre cose, ma non gli erano riuscite. Ieri abbiamo visto Allegri con la faccia giusta”.

L'Inter pensa già al futuro sul mercato e sta già sondando i nomi da poter aggiungere all'organico attuale per renderlo ancora più competitivo. E, secondo TMW, l'attenzione del club nerazzurra è rivolta in Premier League, in particolare all'Arsenal: "Per rinforzare la linea a tre di Cristian Chivu, gli uomini di mercato continuano a guardare con grande attenzione in casa Arsenal, dove due profili di spessore stanno trovando poco spazio a causa della folta concorrenza londinese: Piero Hincapié e Cristhian Mosquera.

Recent findings suggest that L’ecuadoriano, 24 anni e mancino puro, ha raccolto finora appena 9 presenze e 374 minuti complessivi. Abituato alla difesa a tre con cui gioca stabilmente in nazionale, garantirebbe rapidità nei recuperi, impostazione pulita e una preziosa duttilità, potendo agire sia da perno centrale che da vice Bastoni. Lo spagnolo Mosquera, classe 2004, centrale destro dalla stazza imponente e dominante nel gioco aereo, è fermo invece a 5 apparizioni per 169 minuti totali: per prestanza fisica e letture preventive rappresenterebbe l’erede ideale al centro del reparto.

Entrambi i giocatori spingono per avere maggiore minutaggio e continuità. Se la dirigenza nerazzurra deciderà di affondare il colpo, la formula giusta per convincere i Gunners potrebbe essere quella del prestito con obbligo di riscatto, fissato intorno ai 40-45 milioni di euro per Hincapié e ai 35 milioni per Mosquera. Difficile, tuttavia, che l’operazione possa decollare già nella finestra di gennaio: ogni discorso è rimandato a giugno, quando l’acquisto di un difensore di livello internazionale diventerà una priorità assoluta per il club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22.

Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.

The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.

For the second successive campaign, the Timbers face a must-win situation heading into game two of the playoffs after lacking decisiveness in the attacking third last Saturday.

Portland have not made it beyond the opening round of the playoffs since their run to the MLS Cup final in 2021, losing to Fresh York City FC on penalties that year.

They are now 12-10-8 all-time in post-season outings, while winning just one of their last seven playoff games in normal time.

That said, Marti Cifuentes has seen his side lose just one of their last six league fixtures at Providence Park, winning those last two matches and scoring three goals both times.

In addition to that, this club have gone on to win their last two post-season matches at home, while suffering just one playoff defeat this decade at Providence Park in 90 minutes.

The Timbers have never lost a playoff home game versus Dallas in normal time, though their last post-season win against them at Providence Park occurred in 2015 (3-1).

After a cagey opening 45 minutes in game one, Dallas took command in the second half last week, putting themselves in the driver’s seat to advance.

Whatever Eric Quill is saying to this group at half-time, the message has been well received, with his team outscoring opponents by a combined 6-1 margin in the second half of their last two games.

A triumph on Saturday would snap a three-match MLS winless run for the Texas club away from home and mark their first playoff victory as the visitors since beating the Timbers on penalties in Portland in 2020.

Since that triumph, Dallas have failed to score in four of their last five post-season affairs which took place outside of Frisco.

In 2026, they have conceded in all but three MLS road outings, while allowing three or more goals on four separate occasions.

Los Toros can extend their winning run versus Portland to three matches on Saturday, while they are unbeaten in eight successive meetings against them.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:.

Dallas Major League Soccer form:.

Do not expect to see Juan David Mosquera on the field for the Timbers Saturday as he recovers from a foot and ankle issue, while Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is dealing with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful due to a shoulder strain.

Cole Bassett and Kristoffer Velde were the most dangerous Portland players in game one, each with three shots, while James Pantemis made five stops in a losing effort.

At Dallas, Anderson Julio is questionable for this match because of a lower-body injury after sitting out in the opening game of this series.

Joaquin Valiente registered his first career playoff brace in game one, with Sam Sarver scoring his first MLS post-season goal in that victory.

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:.

Pantemis; Hernandez, K. Miller, Waterman, Fory; Bassett, Chara, Da Costa; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter.

Dallas possible starting lineup:.

Daniel; Johansson, Urhoghide, Moore, Norris; Valiente, Kaick, Ramiro, Binyamin; Musa, Sarver.

Dallas tend to sit back away from home, and while their defensive shape will be tough to break down, we believe the Timbers' attacking depth and desperation will keep them alive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:29, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:59.

For the first time in club history, St Louis City can advance beyond the opening round of the MLS playoffs with a victory over Los Angeles FC on Saturday at BMO Stadium.

Game one of this best-of-three series went the way of St Louis, who hung on to a 3-2 triumph at home on Monday night.

It was another case of too little too late for Los Angeles in game one, as they netted twice in the final 45 minutes, which was ultimately not enough.

The last six MLS goals scored by Xavi Tamarit’s men have occurred in the second half, three with fewer than 10 minutes remaining.

They enter this must-win encounter on a five-match winless run in MLS, while winning just one of their last four league games at home.

On the other hand, LAFC have only suffered one defeat in their last six league fixtures on home soil, while boasting a 100% record at BMO Stadium since the introduction of this best-of-three opening round format.

Overall, the Black and Gold have won eight playoff games at home in their history while suffering only one defeat in 11 games.

Saturday will mark the fifth time they host St Louis City with LAFC unbeaten against them at home, winning three of those matches.

The two-week break in between Decision Day and the start of the post-season seemed to do St Louis City a world of good.

Yoann Demet’s men looked a lot more like themselves than we had seen of late, winning a second successive MLS outing in game one after losing four in a row before that.

This upcoming match will only be their second playoff game away from home, after the club lost 2-1 at Sporting Kansas City in 2023.

Two of their last three domestic away matches ended in defeat, and this team have given up multiple goals on the road in seven MLS outings this year.

During the 2026 regular season, St Louis City failed to win four times away from home when netting the opening goal, though they only lost in one of those instances (3-2 at Minnesota United).

While they have yet to beat LAFC outside of Energizer Park, St Louis City have won their last two league games in California, defeating the San Jose Earthquakes and Los Angeles Galaxy during the regular season.

Los Angeles FC Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City form (all competitions):.

Due to a pelvic glitch, Timothy Tillman is questionable for Los Angeles, Jacob Shaffelburg is doubtful with a chest injury, while Thayllon and Tyler Boyd are both unlikely to feature because of leg injuries and Hugo Lloris was back between the sticks for game one.

Sergi Palencia pulled a goal back for them in St Louis the last time out, and Denis Bouanga netted a late one from the penalty spot, drawing even with Jordan Morris for the most playoff goals (11) among active MLS players.

As for St Louis, Celio Pompeu and Carlo Holse are both doubtful with knee injuries, while Roman Burki was back between the sticks in the opening game of this series.

Daniel Edelman, Jeong Sang-bin and Simon Becher all scored their first career MLS playoff goals in their game one triumph, with the latter netting with 12 minutes remaining.

Los Angeles FC possible starting lineup:.

Lloris; Palencia, Porteous, Segura, Cheberko; Choiniere, Delgado; Walta, Heung-min, Bouanga; Sieb.

St Louis City possible starting lineup:.

Burki; MacNaughton, Baumgartl, Polvara; Wallem, Durkin, Edelman, Totland; Sang-bin, Navarro, Matan.

As poor as LAFC have been, we expect their experience in these moments to shine through in game two against a St Louis City team who might take their foot off the gas, knowing they are guaranteed at least one more game no matter what.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
  • La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.
  • Industry observers note that la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

Industry observers note that la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

Recent findings suggest that ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/.

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

Recent findings suggest that I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

Questi i prezzi della Tribuna Family:.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE).

In a recent development, dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM.

It has been revealed that dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

FASE 2 – ISCRIZIONE PREMIUM SSC NAPOLI.

Dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

Recent findings suggest that in caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

Per maggiori informazioni sulla modalità Passbook consultare questo link (si apre in una nuova scheda).

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita è vietata ai residenti nella regione Lombardia, ad eccezione dei possessori di Fidelity Card SSC Napoli emessa entro il 1° settembre 2026.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/.

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD).

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (793 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Industry observers note that morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS stated: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:34.

In a recent development, needing a win to stay alive in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs, the Philadelphia Union will welcome the New England Revolution to Subaru Park for game two of that opening-round series. on Saturday.

A 2-0 win at Foxborough has the Revs one triumph away from getting into the second round of the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

More than ever, the Union must show the resilience we have seen throughout the 2026 campaign if they are to remain in the MLS playoffs.

In game one, Philly fielded the youngest starting 11 in MLS playoff history, averaging 23 years and 207 days, and that inexperience revealed at times as they fired just two targeted efforts in 90 minutes.

Ryan Richter’s men have lost two of their last three league outings but have never suffered consecutive defeats since he took charge.

Since their fresh coach was brought in on an interim basis, the team have won eight of their last 11 MLS games at home, with just one defeat over that stretch.

Philly have gone on to lose only one post-season outing at Subaru Park since the start of the 2022 playoffs, with New York City FC beating them 1-0 in the conference semi-finals a year ago.

Historically, this team have never lost game two in this best-of-three playoff format, failing to concede in those two previous such outings.

A wait of over three years since their last post-season appearance was well worth it for Revs fans last weekend, who saw their team win a playoff game for the first time since 2020.

Should they triumph this weekend, they would advance beyond their first playoff opponent for the first time since 2020, when they reached the Eastern Conference Final.

Newly introduced England have not won a post-season away game since then, and on Saturday can avoid suffering successive MLS away defeats for the first time since losing their first three road games of the 2026 regular season.

Marko Mitrovic is the fifth coach in club history to make the playoffs in his first season at the helm, and the Serbian can become the first Revs manager to triumph in his first MLS post-season away outing this century.

The Revs have never won game two since this best-of-three format was introduced in 2023, losing 1-0 in this exact spot at home to the Union that year.

At the same time, New England can extend their winning run versus Philly to four matches this weekend and win a playoff away game against them for the first time since 2020 (2-0).

Latest England Revolution Major League Soccer form:.

A concussion could keep Japhet Sery Larsen and Finn Sundstrum out of game two for the Union, while Alejandro Bedoya is questionable with an eye injury and Andre Blake is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Cavan Sullivan had a brace in their last home match of the regular season, and the promising youngster will seek his first-ever MLS playoff goal this weekend.

On the Revolution side, Griffin Yow and Leonardo Campana are both expected to miss this match with lower-body injuries.

Peyton Miller scored his career post-season goal in game one, with Nathan Harriel’s early own goal holding up as the winner, while Carles Gil picked up his sixth career postseason assist.

Philadelphia Union possible starting lineup:.

Rick; Westfield, Pierre, Harriel, Wagner; C. Sullivan, Jean Jacques, Lukic, Q. Sullivan; Damiani, Iloski.

Turner; Feingold, Kohler, Wynder, Sands; Gil, Polster, Raines; Miller, Turgeman, Gazdag.

Charlotte FC can book a place in the second round of the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time in club history with a Saturday home win over the Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium.

A thrilling 2-1 triumph in game one last Sunday has the Crown in line to capture their first playoff series with another win this weekend.

They needed to battle until the bitter end of game one, but ultimately Charlotte got the job done, scoring the winner in the 12th minute of stoppage time.

That was the first-ever playoff victory for this team in normal time, while they have never won a post-season outing at Bank of America Stadium in 90 minutes.

Coming into this upcoming match, Charlotte are unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs, while netting multiple goals in six straight domestic games.

Dean Smith’s men have not lost a single league fixture at home in 2026 when netting in the opening half, dropping points in only one of those instances all year.

This weekend they will seek a third successive MLS triumph at Bank of America Stadium and can end a two-game playoff losing run on home soil.

The Crown have netted just once in their three post-season outings at home, while conceding a combined four goals over that stretch.

Chicago have failed to keep their composure in the latter stages of matches recently, and that has them on the verge of an early playoff exit.

Gregg Berhalter’s men have conceded a stoppage-time winner in their last two MLS affairs, while allowing five goals domestically beyond 90 minutes this year.

To prolong this series to a deciding game three, they must do something they have not done in over 20 years, win a post-season match away from home, with their last one coming in 2006 at the Newly introduced England Revolution (1-0).

That said, the Fire have won their last two league fixtures as the visitors, scoring a combined seven goals over that stretch.

They have not scored an opening-half playoff goal since a 2-0 win at home over the Revolution in the 2009 Eastern Conference Semi-finals.

On the other hand, the Fire can claim a third successive triumph at Bank of America Stadium on Saturday, blanking them 1-0 in Charlotte in September.

Victor Munoz injury revision: Andoni Iraola latest on 'painful' glitch as Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in Champions League

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 01:57.
  • Victor Munoz was optimistic that he avoided serious injury for Liverpool against Club Brugge, head coach Andoni Iraola has confirmed.
  • The Reds boss oversaw a 3-0 victory on Wednesday against Brugge, with the three points ensuring the Merseysiders climbed to fifth in the Champions League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 01:57.

Victor Munoz was optimistic that he avoided serious injury for Liverpool against Club Brugge, head coach Andoni Iraola has confirmed.

The Reds boss oversaw a 3-0 victory on Wednesday against Brugge, with the three points ensuring the Merseysiders climbed to fifth in the Champions League table.

While there were several positives to take from the game, winger Munoz was forced off before half time, with the 23-year-old having seemingly damaged his knee.

In a recent development, speaking to reporters after the match, Iraola confirmed that Munoz was positive about his injury, saying: "[Munoz's injury] is the worst part of the game, definitely. He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch.

He was a lot more positive when the game had finished. It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it's just this knock, but obviously it's very early to tell if there is something more than the knock.

Industry observers note that "In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.".

Munoz has already suffered one knee injury this season, so fans will hope that the winger has not suffered a potentially more serious setback.

There is a chance that Munoz could be ready for the Merseyside derby against Everton on Sunday, though it would be safer to assume that he will miss out.

If the winger has suffered a Grade 1 problem, then he may only miss one to three weeks of action, though three weeks on the treatment table would still see him ruled out for up to six games.

A Grade 2 injury would involve a partial tear of ligament or tissue, and that would leave the Spaniard unavailable for up to six weeks.

Liverpool will hope that Munoz has avoided anything more serious given a Grade 3 injury would require months of treatment.

Cody Gakpo is also sidelined because of a calf issue, meaning the only fit wingers at Anfield are Bradley Barcola and Rio Ngumoha.

The latter cannot be expected to play every game considering he is only 18, so it is understandable that some fans have called for January reinforcements.

However, signing another forward could block Ngumoha's pathway to the first team, especially once Gakpo and Munoz return, so it may be better to keep the attacking line as it is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

It has been revealed that alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Sources indicate that palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

In a recent development, when it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

Sources indicate that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Recent findings suggest that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

In a recent development, reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who stated: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

Sources indicate that “I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

In a recent development, any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Sources indicate that valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers notes he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

Industry observers note that here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

Industry observers note that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he remarked: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

In a recent development, on Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady mentioned on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the significant guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

According to recent reports, A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.
